units.zh: 列傳二百五十二
units.en: Biographies 252
units.literal: Biographies 252

units.zh: 徐桐 剛毅 趙舒翹 啟秀 英年 裕祿 毓賢。
units.en: Xu Tong; Gang Yi; Zhao Shuqiao; Qi Xiu; Ying Nian; Yu Lu; Yu Xian.
units.literal: Xu Tong, Gang Yi, Zhao Shuqiao, Qi Xiu, Ying Nian, Yu Lu, Yu Xian.

units.zh: 徐桐，字蔭軒，漢軍正藍旗人，尚書澤醇子。
units.en: Xu Tong, whose style was Yinxuan, came from the Plain Blue Banner of the Han Chinese Banners; his father was Minister Ze Chun.
units.literal: Xu Tong, styled Yinxuan, was a man of the Plain Blue Banner of the Han Chinese Banners and son of Minister Ze Chun.

units.zh: 道光三十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: In 1850 he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
units.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin, and appointed compiler.

units.zh: 坐修改中卷干磨勘，罷職。
units.en: He was dismissed after altering an examination middle scroll and being caught in a review.
units.literal: Because he altered the middle scroll in an examination and was caught in a review, he was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 咸豐十年，特賞檢討，協修文宗實錄。
units.en: In 1860 he was specially made a reviser and helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he was specially granted the post of reviser and helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong.

units.zh: 同治初，命在上書房行走，奉懿旨番講治平寶鑑，入直弘德殿，累遷侍講學士。
units.en: Early in the Tongzhi reign he served in the Upper Study Halls, lectured on the Mirror of Governance and Tranquility by empress-dowager order, entered duty at Hongde Hall, and rose to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he was ordered to serve in the Upper Study Halls, received an empress-dowager edict to lecture on the Mirror of Governance and Tranquility, entered duty at Hongde Hall, and was promoted step by step to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

units.zh: 先後疏請習政事、勤修省，成大學衍義體要以進。
units.en: He repeatedly urged study of government and diligent self-examination, and presented his Essentials of the Great Learning in Outline.
units.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to study state affairs and practice diligent self-examination, and completed the Essentials of the Great Learning in Outline to present.

units.zh: 數擢至禮部侍郎。
units.en: He was promoted several times to Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: He was promoted several times to Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 念外人麕集京師，和議難恃，宜壹意修攘圖自強；
units.en: Seeing foreigners massed in the capital and treaties unreliable, he argued the court should focus on defense and self-strengthening;
units.literal: Reflecting that foreigners thronged the capital and peace negotiations could not be relied on, he held that one should concentrate on strengthening defenses and plotting self-strengthening;

units.zh: 因條上簡才能、結民心、裕度支、修邊備四策。
units.en: he proposed four policies: appointing capable men, winning popular support, strengthening finances, and repairing frontier defenses.
units.literal: he therefore itemized four policies: selecting talent, binding popular hearts, expanding revenue, and repairing frontier defenses.

units.zh: 光緒初，授禮部尚書，加太子少保。
units.en: Early in the Guangxu reign he became Minister of Rites with the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he was appointed Minister of Rites and given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 主事吳可讀請豫定大統，以屍諫，桐與翁同龢等謂其未悉本朝家法：「當申明列聖不建儲彝訓，俾知他日紹膺大寶之元良，即為承繼穆宗之聖子。
units.en: When Principal Clerk Wu Kedu petitioned to settle the succession in advance and died remonstrating, Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe argued he misunderstood dynastic law: "The ancestral rule against naming an heir in advance should be reaffirmed, so all would know the heir who one day receives the throne is the son who succeeds Emperor Muzong.
units.literal: Principal Clerk Wu Kedu requested that the succession be settled in advance and remonstrated with his corpse; Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe and others said he did not understand the house law of the dynasty: "The instruction of successive sages not to establish an heir in advance ought to be declared, so that people may know the heir apparent who will one day receive the great treasure is the sage son who will succeed Emperor Muzong.

units.zh: 揆諸前諭則合，準諸家法則符。」
units.en: That accords with prior edicts and with house law."
units.literal: Measured against earlier edicts it accords; judged by house law it conforms."

units.zh: 疏入，詔存毓慶宮備覽。
units.en: The memorial was filed and the throne ordered it kept in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration for reference.
units.literal: When the memorial entered, an edict ordered it kept in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration for reference.

units.zh: 時擅訂約，下群臣議，乃條摘其不可行者：曰、各城定界；
units.en: When Chonghou took it upon himself to negotiate the Russian treaty, the matter was laid before the full court. Xu Tong listed the terms that could not be accepted: delimiting the cities of Ili and Tarbagatai;
units.literal: At that time Chonghou had arbitrarily concluded a treaty with Russia; when it was referred to the court for discussion among all officials, [Xu Tong] itemized what could not be accepted: namely, fixing boundaries for the cities of Ili and Tarbagatai;

units.zh: 曰新疆、蒙古通商；
units.en: opening trade in Xinjiang and Mongolia;
units.literal: namely, opening trade in Xinjiang and Mongolia;

units.zh: 曰運貨迳至漢口；
units.en: allowing cargo to pass through to Hankou;
units.literal: namely, transporting goods straight through to Hankou;

units.zh: 曰行船直入伯都訥。
units.en: and permitting vessels to navigate directly to Berdunier.
units.literal: namely, permitting ships to sail directly into Berdunier.

units.zh: 六年，廷議徇俄人請，將赦崇厚罪，桐力持不可，謂：「揆度機要在樞廷，折衝俎豆在總署，講信修睦在使臣。
units.en: In 1880, when the court debated yielding to Russian pressure and pardoning Chonghou, Xu Tong stood firm against it, arguing: "Strategic judgment rests with the Grand Council; negotiation at the council table rests with the Zongli Yamen; building trust and good relations rests with the envoys.
units.literal: In the sixth year, when the court considered acceding to the Russians' request and were about to pardon Chonghou's crime, [Xu] Tong firmly insisted it could not be done, saying: "Weighing strategy belongs in the Grand Council; parrying at the council table belongs in the Zongli Yamen; cultivating trust and harmony belongs to the envoys.

units.zh: 赦之而彼就範，猶裨國事；
units.en: If a pardon brings them to terms, it may still serve the state;
units.literal: If one pardons him and the other side then submits, it may still benefit state affairs;

units.zh: 若釁端仍不能弭，反失刑政大權。
units.en: but if hostilities cannot be settled, we forfeit the crown's authority over punishment and law.
units.literal: but if trouble cannot still be quelled, one instead loses the great authority of penal administration.

units.zh: 推原禍始，宜肅國憲。」
units.en: The root of the disaster should be traced to strict enforcement of national law."
units.literal: Tracing the origin of the calamity, the state constitution ought to be upheld."

units.zh: 又言：「今日用人之道，秉忠持正者為上，宅心樸實者次之。
units.en: He added: "In appointing officials today, men who are loyal and upright should come first; men of plain and honest character should come next.
units.literal: He also said: "The way to employ men today: those who uphold loyalty and rectitude rank first; those whose hearts are plain and honest rank next.

units.zh: 若以機權靈警，諳曉各國語言文字，遽目為通才，而責以鉅任，未有不僨且蹶者！」
units.en: To treat men merely because they are quick-witted and fluent in foreign tongues and scripts as universal talents fit for weighty office is to invite certain ruin."
units.literal: If one suddenly regards men who are sharp in maneuver, clever and alert, and versed in the languages and scripts of the various nations as versatile talents and charges them with great responsibilities, there has never been a case where they did not collapse in failure!"

units.zh: 不報。
units.en: His advice went unheeded.
units.literal: There was no response.

units.zh: 歷充翰林院掌院學士、上書房總師傅。
units.en: He rose to be chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and grand tutor in the Upper Study Halls.
units.literal: He successively served as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Tutor of the Upper Study Halls.

units.zh: 十五年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士，晉太子太保。
units.en: In the fifteenth year (1889) he was appointed Minister of Personnel with concurrent duty as assistant grand secretary, then promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year, as Minister of Personnel he served as Assistant Grand Secretary, and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 二十二年，拜體仁閣大學士。
units.en: In the twenty-second year (1896) he was made grand secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence.

units.zh: 桐崇宋儒說，守舊，惡西學如仇。
units.en: Xu Tong revered Song Neo-Confucianism, clung to the old ways, and hated Western learning like a mortal foe.
units.literal: Xu Tong revered Song Neo-Confucian doctrine, clung to the old ways, and hated Western learning as he would an enemy.

units.zh: 門人言新政者，屏不令入謁。
units.en: He barred disciples who advocated reform from his audience.
units.literal: Disciples who spoke of new policies he barred and would not receive in audience.

units.zh: 二十四年政變後，太后以其耆臣碩望，頗優禮，朝請令近侍扶掖以寵之。
units.en: After the 1898 coup the Empress Dowager favored this venerable statesman, ordering attendants to support him at court.
units.literal: After the coup of the twenty-fourth year the Empress Dowager, because he was an aged minister of great reputation, treated him with especial favor and ordered attendants to support him at court as a mark of grace.

units.zh: 有豫師者，字錫之，內務府漢軍。
units.en: Yu Shi, whose style was Xizhi, served in the Imperial Household Department as a member of the Han Chinese Banner.
units.literal: There was Yu Shi, styled Xizhi, of the Han Chinese Banner in the Imperial Household Department.

units.zh: 進士。
units.en: He held the jinshi degree.
units.literal: A jinshi degree holder.

units.zh: 官至烏魯木齊都統，以講學為桐所傾服。
units.en: He eventually became commander-in-chief at Urumqi, and Xu Tong looked up to him as a scholar.
units.literal: He rose to commandant-general at Urumqi; Xu Tong admired him for his scholarship.

units.zh: 方太后議廢帝，立端王載漪子溥儁為「大阿哥」，桐主之甚力，實皆豫師本謀也。
units.en: During the debate over deposing the emperor and elevating Prince Duan's son Pujun as "Great Heir Apparent," Xu Tong pushed hard for it—the scheme was Yu Shi's in essence.
units.literal: When the Empress Dowager debated deposing the emperor and installing Prince Duan's son Pujun as "Great Heir Apparent," Xu Tong strongly advocated it; in truth all these plots originated with Yu Shi.

units.zh: 既而桐被命照料，益親載漪。
units.en: Once Xu Tong was charged with supervising the boy, he grew even closer to Prince Duan.
units.literal: When Xu Tong was thereafter ordered to oversee [the heir], he became still closer to Prince Duan.

units.zh: 各國不慊載漪等所為，漪恚甚，圖報復。
units.en: The foreign powers were displeased with what Prince Duan and his circle had done; furious, he sought revenge.
units.literal: The foreign powers were displeased with what Prince Duan and his circle had done; furious, he sought revenge.

units.zh: 二十六年，義和拳起釁仇外，載漪大喜，導之入都。
units.en: In 1900, when the Boxers stirred up hatred of foreigners, Prince Duan was delighted and ushered them into Beijing.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Boxers rose and turned hostility outward, [Prince Duan] was greatly pleased and guided them into the capital.

units.zh: 桐謂：「中國當自此強矣！」
units.en: Xu Tong declared: "From this day China will grow strong!"
units.literal: Xu Tong said: "China shall henceforth be strong!"

units.zh: 至且親迓之。
units.en: He even went out in person to welcome them.
units.literal: He would even go out in person to welcome them.

units.zh: 然及其亂時，仍被劫掠。
units.en: Yet when the chaos broke out, he was looted like everyone else.
units.literal: Yet during the disorder he was still plundered.

units.zh: 袁昶、許景澄之死，舉國稱冤，而桐則曰：「是死且有餘辜！」
units.en: When Yuan Chang and Xu Jingcheng were executed, the nation called it a miscarriage of justice; Xu Tong said: "They deserved worse than death!"
units.literal: At the deaths of Yuan Chang and Xu Jingcheng the whole country called it injustice, but Xu Tong said: "Even in death they still had guilt to spare!"

units.zh: 時其子監刑，揚揚頗自得。
units.en: His son Chengyu oversaw the executions, swaggering with evident satisfaction.
units.literal: At the time his son Chengyu supervised the execution, looking quite pleased with himself.

units.zh: 承煜，字楠士。
units.en: Chengyu, whose style was Nanshi.
units.literal: Chengyu, styled Nanshi.

units.zh: 拔貢。
units.en: He had entered by senior licentiate recommendation.
units.literal: A senior licentiate by recommendation.

units.zh: 以戶部小京官晉遷郎中，累官刑部左侍郎。
units.en: He rose from a junior post in the Ministry of Revenue to director and eventually Left Vice Minister of Justice.
units.literal: Starting as a junior secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, he was promoted step by step to director, and eventually rose to Left Vice Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 已，聯軍入，桐倉皇失措，承煜請曰：「父芘拳匪，外人至，必不免，失大臣體。
units.en: When the allied armies entered Beijing, Xu Tong panicked. Chengyu urged him: "Father sheltered the Boxers; when the foreigners arrive you cannot escape without disgracing your rank.
units.literal: Before long the allied armies entered; Xu Tong was flustered and at a loss, and Chengyu urged: "Father sheltered the Boxer bandits; when foreigners arrive you cannot escape and will lose the dignity of a great minister.

units.zh: 盍殉國？
units.en: Why not die for the state?
units.literal: Why not die for the state?

units.zh: 兒當從侍地下耳！」
units.en: Your son will follow you to the grave!"
units.literal: Your son will follow and attend you in the grave!"

units.zh: 桐乃投繯死，年八十有二矣。
units.en: Xu Tong hanged himself at the age of eighty-two.
units.literal: Xu Tong then hanged himself; he was eighty-two.

units.zh: 而承煜遂亡走，為日軍所拘，置之順天府尹署，與啟秀俱明年正月正法。
units.en: Chengyu fled but was seized by Japanese troops and held at the Shuntian prefect's yamen; he and Qi Xiu were executed the following first month.
units.literal: Chengyu then fled, was seized by the Japanese army, and was placed in the yamen of the prefect of Shuntian; he and Qi Xiu were both executed by lawful punishment in the first month of the following year.

units.zh: 命下，日軍官置酒為餞，傳詔旨，承煜色變，口呼冤，痛詆西人不已。
units.en: When the order came, a Japanese officer offered wine and read the edict; Chengyu turned pale, cried injustice, and bitterly denounced the Westerners.
units.literal: When the order came down, a Japanese officer set out wine to send him off and transmitted the edict; Chengyu changed color, cried out his innocence, and bitterly denounced Westerners without cease.

units.zh: 翼日，備輿送至菜市，監刑官出席禮之，已昏不知人矣，尋就戮。
units.en: The next day he was taken to Caishikou; the execution officer saluted him, but he was already unconscious when he was killed.
units.literal: The next day a carriage was prepared to send him to Caishikou; the supervising execution officer came out to salute him, but he was already unconscious; soon he was put to death.

units.zh: 和議成，褫桐職，奪卹典，旋論棄市，以先死議免。
units.en: After peace was made Xu Tong's offices and mourning honors were revoked; public execution was debated but waived because he had already died.
units.literal: When peace was concluded Xu Tong's offices were stripped and mourning honors revoked; soon decapitation and public display were debated, but because he had died first the sentence was waived.

units.zh: 剛毅，字子良，滿洲鑲藍旗人。
units.en: Gang Yi, whose style was Ziliang, came from the Bordered Blue Banner of the Manchus.
units.literal: Gang Yi, styled Ziliang, was a man of the Bordered Blue Banner of the Manchus.

units.zh: 以筆帖式累遷刑部郎中。
units.en: He rose from clerk through successive posts to director in the Ministry of Justice.
units.literal: Starting as a clerk, he was promoted step by step to director in the Ministry of Justice.

units.zh: 諳悉例案，承審浙江餘杭縣民婦葛畢氏案，獲平反，按律定擬，得旨嘉獎。
units.en: Fluent in legal precedent, he handled the case of Ge Bishi, a commoner woman of Yuhang in Zhejiang, secured her exoneration, and drafted a lawful sentence that earned imperial praise.
units.literal: Well versed in precedent cases, he took charge of trying the case of the commoner woman Ge Bishi of Yuhang County, Zhejiang, secured a reversal of judgment, fixed the sentence according to law, and received an imperial commendation.

units.zh: 出為廣東惠潮嘉道，遷江西按察使，調直隸；
units.en: He served as intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong, then became surveillance commissioner in Jiangxi and was transferred to Zhili;
units.literal: He went out as intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong, was transferred to Jiangxi as surveillance commissioner, then to Zhili;

units.zh: 遷廣東布政使，調雲南。
units.en: then treasurer of Guangdong, and finally was posted to Yunnan.
units.literal: was moved to Guangdong as provincial treasurer, then transferred to Yunnan.

units.zh: 光緒十一年，擢山西巡撫。
units.en: In 1885 he was appointed governor of Shanxi.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Guangxu he was promoted to governor of Shanxi.

units.zh: 請設課吏館，手輯牧令須知諸書，分講習，詔飭行各省。
units.en: He proposed an academy for training officials, compiled manuals such as What Magistrates Must Know, organized instruction, and the court ordered every province to adopt the practice.
units.literal: He requested establishment of an officials' training hall, personally compiled such works as What Magistrates Must Know, arranged lectures, and an edict ordered all provinces to follow suit.

units.zh: 治套外屯田，建分段、開渠、設官三策。
units.en: For frontier garrison farming he advanced three policies: parceling land, digging canals, and appointing overseers.
units.literal: For reclaiming garrison farms beyond the pass he proposed three measures: division into sections, opening canals, and appointing officials.

units.zh: 明年，移撫江蘇。
units.en: The following year he was made governor of Jiangsu.
units.literal: The next year he was transferred to govern Jiangsu.

units.zh: 蘇患水祲，先後濬蘊藻河、吳淞江，以工代賑，民德之。
units.en: When Jiangsu was stricken by flood and drought, he dredged the Yunzao and Wusong rivers and used public works as famine relief; the people were grateful.
units.literal: Jiangsu suffered flood and drought; he successively dredged the Yunzao River and the Wusong River, using labor relief in place of charity grain, and the people were grateful.

units.zh: 調廣東。
units.en: He was then transferred to Guangdong.
units.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong.

units.zh: 二十年，召授軍機大臣，補禮部侍郎。
units.en: In 1894 he was recalled to the Grand Council and made Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: In the twentieth year he was summoned and appointed Grand Councilor, with concurrent appointment as Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 二十四年，以工部尚書協辦大學士，疏陳實倉廩，嚴保甲，罷不急官。
units.en: In 1898, as Minister of Works and assistant grand secretary, he memorialized to fill granaries, tighten local security networks, and cut superfluous posts.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, as Minister of Works he served as Assistant Grand Secretary; in memorials he urged filling granaries, tightening the baojia system, and abolishing nonessential offices.

units.zh: 二十五年，按事江南及廣東諸省。
units.en: In 1899 he toured Jiangnan and Guangdong on inspection.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he conducted investigations in Jiangnan and the Guangdong provinces.

units.zh: 迭疏請籌長江防務，籌餉練兵，清理財政，及整頓地方一切事宜，詔皆飭行。
units.en: He sent repeated memorials on Yangtze defenses, military funding and training, fiscal reform, and local administration; the throne ordered every item implemented.
units.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to plan Yangtze defenses, raise funds and train troops, clear up finances, and put in order all local affairs; edicts ordered all to be carried out.

units.zh: 二十六年，拳亂作，命趙舒翹及剛毅馳往近畿一帶查辦解散，及還京覆命，而宣戰詔已先下矣。
units.en: In 1900, when the Boxer uprising erupted, Zhao Shuqiao and Gang Yi were dispatched to the capital outskirts to investigate and disperse the movement; by the time they returned to report, the declaration of war had already been issued.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer disturbance broke out; Zhao Shuqiao and Gang Yi were ordered to hurry to the near capital region to investigate and disband them; when they returned to the capital to report, the war declaration had already been issued.

units.zh: 匪集都城，肆焚殺，時方稱義民，亡敢誰何。
units.en: The rebels massed in the capital, burning and killing at will; hailed as patriotic militia, they went unchecked.
units.literal: The bandits gathered in the capital and wantonly burned and killed; at the time they were called righteous people, and no one dared challenge them.

units.zh: 載漪等復疏言：「雪恥強國，在此一舉！」
units.en: Prince Duan and his allies memorialized again: "National humiliation can be wiped away and the state strengthened in this single stroke!"
units.literal: Zaiyi and others again memorialized: "To wipe away disgrace and strengthen the state—this one stroke suffices!"

units.zh: 又盛推拳民忠勇，有神術，可用。
units.en: They lavishly praised the Boxers as loyal, brave, possessed of magic, and fit for service.
units.literal: They also lavishly praised the Boxers' loyalty and courage, claiming they had divine arts and could be used.

units.zh: 太后愈信之，因命剛毅、載勳統之，比於官軍。
units.en: The Empress Dowager believed them still more and put Gang Yi and Zai Xun in command, treating the Boxers as the equal of regular troops.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager believed them all the more and therefore ordered Gang Yi and Zai Xun to command them, ranking them with the regular army.

units.zh: 然匪專殺自如，勿能問，且擾禁城，日焚劫不止。
units.en: Yet the rebels killed as they pleased, beyond anyone's control, harrying even the Forbidden City with daily arson and looting.
units.literal: Yet the bandits killed as they pleased without restraint; none could call them to account, and they even disturbed the Forbidden City, with burning and looting daily unceasing.

units.zh: 詔各軍營會拏正法，盡拆所設神壇，並諭責剛毅、董福祥親自開導，勒令解散，卒不能阻。
units.en: Edicts ordered every garrison to arrest and execute offenders, tear down their altars, and commanded Gang Yi and Dong Fuxiang personally to disband the movement—yet nothing could stop it.
units.literal: An edict ordered all camps jointly to seize and execute according to law, tear down all altars they had set up, and also rebuked Gang Yi and Dong Fuxiang to guide them in person and compel disbandment—yet in the end they could not stop them.

units.zh: 各國聯軍入犯，兩宮西狩，剛毅扈行至太原。
units.en: When the allied armies invaded, the court fled west; Gang Yi escorted the empresses as far as Taiyuan.
units.literal: When the allied armies of the various nations invaded, the two palaces went west on tour; Gang Yi escorted them as far as Taiyuan.

units.zh: 車駕欲之西安，又從。
units.en: When the court decided to continue to Xi'an, he went along.
units.literal: When the imperial procession wished to go to Xi'an, he followed again.

units.zh: 道遘疾，還至侯馬鎮，死。
units.en: He fell ill on the road, turned back to Houma, and died there.
units.literal: On the road he fell ill, returned to Houma Town, and died.

units.zh: 其後各國請懲禍首，以先死免議，追奪原官。
units.en: Later the powers demanded the chief culprits be punished; his prior death spared formal proceedings, but his offices were posthumously revoked.
units.literal: Afterward the various nations demanded punishment of the chief culprits; because he had died first he was spared discussion, but his former offices were posthumously stripped.

units.zh: 趙舒翹，字展如，陝西長安人。
units.en: Zhao Shuqiao, whose style was Zhanru, came from Chang'an in Shaanxi.
units.literal: Zhao Shuqiao, styled Zhanru, was a native of Chang'an in Shaanxi.

units.zh: 同治十三年進士，授刑部主事，遷員外郎。
units.en: He took his jinshi degree in 1874, entered the Ministry of Justice as a principal clerk, and rose to vice director.
units.literal: A jinshi of the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and was promoted to vice director.

units.zh: 讞河南王樹汶獄，承旨研辨，獲平反，巡撫李鶴年以下譴謫有差。
units.en: In the Henan case of Wang Shuwen he followed imperial orders, secured a reversal, and Governor Li Henian and his subordinates were punished in varying degrees.
units.literal: He reported on the Henan case of Wang Shuwen; following the imperial order he investigated and secured a reversal of judgment, and Governor Li Henian and those below him were censured and demoted to varying degrees.

units.zh: 居刑曹十年，多所纂定，其議服制及婦女離異諸條，能傅古義，為時所誦。
units.en: After ten years in the penal bureaucracy he codified many rules; his treatises on mourning dress and on divorce and separation for women were praised for recovering classical principles.
units.literal: He spent ten years in the penal offices and compiled many regulations; his discussions of mourning garb and of women's divorce and separation could transmit ancient meaning and were recited in his time.

units.zh: 光緒十二年，以郎中出知安徽鳳陽府。
units.en: In 1886 he left the ministry as a director to become prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he went out from his directorship to serve as prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.

units.zh: 皖北水祲，割俸助賑。
units.en: When northern Anhui was stricken by flood and drought, he donated his salary to relief efforts.
units.literal: Northern Anhui suffered flood and drought; he cut his salary to aid relief.

units.zh: 課最，擢浙江溫處道，再遷布政使。
units.en: Rated top in performance reviews, he was made intendant of Wenzhou and Taizhou in Zhejiang, then provincial treasurer.
units.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, he was promoted to intendant of Wenzhou and Taichou in Zhejiang, then again transferred to provincial treasurer.

units.zh: 二十年，擢江蘇巡撫。
units.en: In 1894 he was appointed governor of Jiangsu.
units.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor of Jiangsu.

units.zh: 捕治太湖匪酋葉子春，餘黨股栗；
units.en: He captured the Lake Tai bandit leader Ye Zichun, and the remaining gangs trembled;
units.literal: He captured and punished the bandit chieftain Ye Zichun on Lake Tai; the remaining gangs trembled;

units.zh: 復為籌善後策，弊風漸革。
units.en: he devised follow-up policies, and local abuses were gradually curbed.
units.literal: he also devised policies for aftermath, and corrupt practices were gradually reformed.

units.zh: 明年，改訂日本條約，牒請總署重民生，所言皆切中。
units.en: The next year, during revision of the Japanese treaty, he urged the Zongli Yamen to put the people's livelihood first—every point he made was on target.
units.literal: The next year, when the treaty with Japan was revised, he memorialized the Zongli Yamen to stress livelihood of the people; everything he said hit the mark.

units.zh: 是時朝廷矜慎庶獄，以舒翹諳律令，召為刑部左侍郎。
units.en: The court was then cautious about ordinary criminal cases and recalled him as Left Vice Minister of Justice for his mastery of law.
units.literal: At that time the court was cautious about common criminal cases; because Shuqiao was versed in statutes, he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 二十四年，晉尚書，督辦礦務、鐵路。
units.en: In 1898 he was promoted to minister and placed in charge of mining and railways.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to minister and supervised mining and railways.

units.zh: 明年，命入總理各國事務衙門，充軍機大臣。
units.en: The following year he entered the Zongli Yamen and joined the Grand Council.
units.literal: The next year he was ordered into the Zongli Yamen and appointed Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 拳匪據涿州，舒翹被命馳往解散；
units.en: When the Boxers occupied Zhuozhou, Shuqiao was sent to disperse them;
units.literal: When the Boxers seized Zhuozhou, Shuqiao was ordered to hurry there to disband them;

units.zh: 匪眾堅請褫提督聶士成職，剛毅踵至，許之。
units.en: the rebels demanded Grand Commissioner Nie Shicheng be removed; Gang Yi arrived after him and agreed.
units.literal: the bandits firmly demanded dismissal of Grand Commissioner Nie Shicheng; Gang Yi followed and granted it.

units.zh: 匪既入京，攻使館。
units.en: Once the rebels entered Beijing they besieged the legations.
units.literal: Once the bandits entered the capital they attacked the legations.

units.zh: 聯軍至，李秉衡兵敗，太后乃令王文韶與舒翹詣使館通殷勤，為議款計。
units.en: When the allied armies arrived and Li Bingheng's force was routed, the Empress Dowager ordered Wang Wenshao and Shuqiao to visit the legations with courtesies to open peace talks.
units.literal: When the allied armies arrived and Li Bingheng's troops were defeated, the Empress Dowager then ordered Wang Wenshao and Shuqiao to go to the legations with courteous messages as a plan to negotiate terms.

units.zh: 文韶以老辭，舒翹曰：「臣望淺，不如文韶！」
units.en: Wenshao pleaded old age; Shuqiao said: "My standing is too slight—I am no match for Wenshao!"
units.literal: Wenshao declined on account of age; Shuqiao said: "Your servant's standing is slight—I am not the equal of Wenshao!"

units.zh: 卒不往。
units.en: In the end he never went.
units.literal: In the end he did not go.

units.zh: 旋隨扈至西安。
units.en: He soon followed the court's flight to Xi'an.
units.literal: Soon afterward he followed the imperial procession to Xi'an.

units.zh: 聯軍索辦罪魁，乃褫職留任，尋改斬監候。
units.en: When the allies demanded the chief culprits be punished, he was stripped of rank but kept under detention, then sentenced to imprisonment awaiting execution.
units.literal: When the allied armies demanded punishment of the chief culprits, he was stripped of office but kept on duty, then changed to imprisonment awaiting decapitation.

units.zh: 次年，各國索益亟，西安士民集數百人為舒翹請命，上聞，賜自盡，命岑春煊監視。
units.en: The next year the powers pressed harder; hundreds of Xi'an residents petitioned for his life, but the throne ordered him to take his own life under Cen Chunxuan's supervision.
units.literal: The next year the various nations pressed their demands more urgently; several hundred gentry and commoners of Xi'an gathered to plead for Shuqiao's life; when this reached the throne he was granted suicide, with Cen Chunxuan ordered to supervise.

units.zh: 舒翹故不袒匪，又痛老母九十餘見此慘禍，頗自悔恨。
units.en: Shuqiao had never openly sided with the Boxers, yet he was tormented that his mother, past ninety, should see this tragedy, and he bitterly repented.
units.literal: Shuqiao had never openly sided with the bandits, yet he also grieved that his mother, over ninety, should witness this calamity, and he deeply repented.

units.zh: 初飲金，更飲以鴆，久之乃絕，其妻仰藥以殉。
units.en: He first swallowed gold, then was given poison; death came only after a long struggle, and his wife took poison to join him.
units.literal: At first he drank gold; then he was given poison; only after a long while did he expire, and his wife took medicine and died with him.

units.zh: 啟秀，字穎之，庫雅拉氏，滿洲正白旗人。
units.en: Qi Xiu, whose style was Yingzhi, came from the Kuyala clan of the Plain White Banner.
units.literal: Qi Xiu, styled Yingzhi, of the Kuyala clan, was a man of the Plain White Banner of the Manchus.

units.zh: 以孝聞。
units.en: He was famed for filial devotion.
units.literal: He was known for filial piety.

units.zh: 同治四年進士，選庶吉士，散館改刑部主事，累遷內閣學士。
units.en: He took his jinshi in 1865, entered the Hanlin Academy, then the Ministry of Justice, and rose to grand secretariat bachelor.
units.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Tongzhi, he was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin, and after leaving the academy was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, rising step by step to a bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.

units.zh: 光緒五年，授工部右侍郎，調盛京刑部。
units.en: In 1879 he became Right Vice Minister of Works and was transferred to the Mukden penal administration.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Works and transferred to the Penal Department of Mukden.

units.zh: 吉林將軍銘​​安被彈劾，啟秀白其誣，轉戶部。
units.en: When General Ming'an of Jilin was impeached, Qi Xiu cleared him of false charges and was moved to the Ministry of Revenue.
units.literal: When General Ming'an of Jilin was impeached, Qi Xiu declared his innocence and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 論者以按銘安事多徇芘，攻甚力，命崇綺覆按，無左驗，免議。
units.en: Critics accused him of favoritism in the Ming'an case; Chongqi reinvestigated, found no proof, and Qi Xiu escaped punishment.
units.literal: Critics held that in handling Ming'an's case he had often shown favoritism and attacked him fiercely; Chongqi was ordered to reinvestigate, found no corroborating evidence, and he was spared censure.

units.zh: 東省練新軍，倚餉京師，閻敬銘掌戶部，方規節帑，未應也。
units.en: Eastern provinces were raising new armies and depended on Beijing for pay; Yan Jingming at the Ministry of Revenue was cutting expenses and had not yet approved the funds.
units.literal: The eastern provinces were training new armies and relied on funds from the capital; Yan Jingming controlled the Ministry of Revenue and was planning to economize the treasury, and had not yet responded.

units.zh: 啟秀力言，始獲請，歲發四十萬濟之。
units.en: Qi Xiu pressed the case until approval came: four hundred thousand taels a year were allocated.
units.literal: Qi Xiu spoke forcefully and only then obtained approval; four hundred thousand taels were sent yearly to support them.

units.zh: 二十年，拜理籓院尚書。
units.en: In 1894 he was made Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
units.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

units.zh: 中、日和議成，將換約，啟秀疏請：「條約宜緩發，先商諸各國，杜後患。」
units.en: When the Sino-Japanese peace was concluded and ratification neared, Qi Xiu urged: "Ratification should be delayed until other powers are consulted, to forestall future trouble."
units.literal: When the Sino-Japanese peace was concluded and the treaty was to be exchanged, Qi Xiu memorialized: "The treaty ought to be issued slowly; first consult the various nations to forestall later troubles."

units.zh: 不報。
units.en: His advice went unheeded.
units.literal: There was no response.

units.zh: 敖漢王達木林達爾達克鑑朝陽覆轍，自請增練蒙軍。
units.en: The Prince of Aohan, Damulin Da'erdake, seeing Chaoyang's troubles repeat, volunteered to expand Mongol troop training.
units.literal: The Prince of Aohan, Damulin Da'erdake, seeing Chaoyang's repeated disasters, requested on his own to increase training of Mongol troops.

units.zh: 言者論其苛派蒙眾，謀不軌，啟秀為訟其冤。
units.en: Critics charged him with extorting the Mongols and plotting rebellion; Qi Xiu defended him.
units.literal: Memorialists argued that he harshly levied on the Mongol populace and plotted sedition; Qi Xiu pleaded his innocence.

units.zh: 敖漢王雖奪扎薩克秩，而其子獲嗣，以故大得蒙眾心。
units.en: Though the prince lost his jasak title, his son inherited it, and he retained strong support among the Mongols.
units.literal: Although the Prince of Aohan was stripped of his jasak rank, his son succeeded to it; for this reason he greatly won the hearts of the Mongol masses.

units.zh: 充總管內務府大臣。
units.en: He became superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
units.literal: He served as superintendent grand minister of the Imperial Household Department.

units.zh: 二十四年，授禮部尚書，疏陳釐正文體，倡明聖學。
units.en: In 1898 he was made Minister of Rites and memorialized to reform literary style and promote classical learning.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Minister of Rites; in memorials he urged correcting literary forms and promoting sagely learning.

units.zh: 命充軍機大臣兼總理各國事務衙門。
units.en: He was appointed to the Grand Council and the Zongli Yamen.
units.literal: He was ordered to serve as Grand Councilor with concurrent duty in the Zongli Yamen.

units.zh: 啟秀端謹有風操，為徐桐所賞。
units.en: Qi Xiu was upright and principled, and Xu Tong held him in high regard.
units.literal: Qi Xiu was upright, careful, and possessed moral integrity; Xu Tong admired him.

units.zh: 自政變後，桐最被盻遇，欲引參機務，乃舉啟秀自代。
units.en: After the 1898 coup Xu Tong was the Empress Dowager's favorite; wanting a proxy in policy, he recommended Qi Xiu to take his place.
units.literal: After the political coup Xu Tong was most favored; wishing to draw him into state affairs, he recommended Qi Xiu to replace himself.

units.zh: 已而拳亂作，董福祥攻使館不下，啟秀薦五台僧禦敵，頗附和之。
units.en: When the Boxer rising erupted and Dong Fuxiang failed to overrun the legations, Qi Xiu recommended a Wutai monk to fight the foreigners and lent his support.
units.literal: Soon the Boxer disturbance broke out; Dong Fuxiang could not take the legations; Qi Xiu recommended a monk of Wutai to repel the enemy and largely went along with the plan.

units.zh: 逮兩宮狩西安，啟秀以母病弗克從。
units.en: When the court fled to Xi'an, Qi Xiu stayed behind because his mother was ill.
units.literal: When the two palaces went on tour to Xi'an, Qi Xiu could not follow because his mother was ill.

units.zh: 日本軍拘啟秀及徐承煜嚴守之，承煜，桐子也。
units.en: Japanese troops seized Qi Xiu and Xu Chengyu and held them under close guard; Chengyu was Xu Tong's son.
units.literal: The Japanese army detained Qi Xiu and Xu Chengyu and kept them under strict guard; Chengyu was Xu Tong's son.

units.zh: 朝旨褫職，而各國猶言罪魁不可縱。
units.en: The court stripped them of rank, but the powers insisted the chief culprits must not go unpunished.
units.literal: An imperial order stripped them of office, yet the various nations still said the chief culprits could not be spared.

units.zh: 明年，正法命下，日軍官置酒為餞，席次，傳詔旨，啟秀神色自若，曰：​​「即此已邀聖恩矣！」
units.en: The following year the execution order came down. A Japanese officer gave him a farewell feast; when the edict was read, Qi Xiu remained composed and said: "Even this is already imperial favor!"
units.literal: The next year the order for lawful execution was issued; a Japanese officer set out wine as a farewell; at the banquet, when the edict was announced, Qi Xiu's expression was calm as he said: "Even this already invites imperial grace!"

units.zh: 肅衣冠赴菜市。
units.en: He dressed in full court robes and walked to the execution ground at Caishikou.
units.literal: He put on formal dress and hat and went to the Vegetable Market.

units.zh: 啟秀宅近日本權領地，日官與語，當善芘其家，第曰：「厚意可感。」
units.en: His home lay near the Japanese concession; a Japanese official promised to protect his family. Qi Xiu replied only: "Your kindness moves me."
units.literal: Qi Xiu's residence was near the Japanese concession; a Japanese official spoke with him, saying his family would be well protected; he only said: "Your generous intent is deeply felt."

units.zh: 他無復言，遂就戮。
units.en: He said nothing more and went to his death.
units.literal: He said nothing more and then submitted to execution.

units.zh: 英年，字菊儕，姓何氏，隸內務府，為漢軍正白旗人。
units.en: Ying Nian, whose style was Juyi, came from the He clan of the Han Chinese Plain White Banner and served in the Imperial Household Department.
units.literal: Ying Nian, styled Juyi, bore the surname He, was attached to the Imperial Household Department, and was a man of the Han Chinese Plain White Banner.

units.zh: 以貢生考取筆帖式，累遷郎中兼護軍參領。
units.en: He entered service as a tribute student, passed the clerk examination, and rose to director with a concurrent post as guard adjutant.
units.literal: As a tribute student he passed the examination for clerk and was promoted step by step to director with concurrent duty as adjutant of the guard.

units.zh: 光緒中，歷奉宸苑卿、左翼總兵、正紅旗漢軍副都統、工部右侍郎，調戶部。
units.en: Under Guangxu he held posts including Director of the Imperial Parks, Left Wing commander-in-chief, vice commander of the Han Chinese Bordered Red Banner, and Right Vice Minister of Works before moving to the Ministry of Revenue.
units.literal: During Guangxu he successively served as Director of the Imperial Parks, Left Wing Commander-in-Chief, Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Han Chinese Bordered Red Banner, and Right Vice Minister of Works, then was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 拳匪亂作，以英年、載瀾副載勳、剛毅統之。
units.en: When the Boxer rising erupted, Ying Nian and Zai Lan were appointed deputies to Zai Xun and Gang Yi in commanding the movement.
units.literal: When the Boxer disturbance broke out, Ying Nian and Zai Lan were made deputies to Zai Xun and Gang Yi to command them.

units.zh: 載勳等出示，招致義民助攻使館，英年弗能阻，匪益橫，任意戕殺官民。
units.en: Zai Xun and his allies posted notices recruiting militia to attack the legations; Ying Nian could not stop them, and the rebels grew bolder, slaughtering officials and civilians at will.
units.literal: Zai Xun and others posted notices and summoned righteous people to assist in attacking the legations; Ying Nian could not stop them, and the bandits grew still more arrogant, killing officials and commoners at will.

units.zh: 聯軍既陷京師，兩宮幸西安，英年充行在查營大臣，旋授左都御史。
units.en: After Beijing fell, the court fled to Xi'an; Ying Nian served as traveling inspector of camps and was soon made Left Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: After the allied armies took the capital, the two palaces went to Xi'an; Ying Nian served as traveling inspector of camps and was soon appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 行次猗氏，知縣玉寶供張不備，疏劾之。
units.en: At Yishi he found Magistrate Yubao's arrangements for the imperial procession inadequate and impeached him.
units.literal: Passing through Yishi, he found the magistrate Yubao's provisions for the imperial procession inadequate and memorialized to impeach him.

units.zh: 款成，各使議懲首禍，英年褫職論斬，羈西安獄，尋賜自盡。
units.en: After peace was made the foreign ministers demanded punishment of the ringleaders; Ying Nian was stripped of rank, sentenced to death, imprisoned in Xi'an, and soon ordered to take his own life.
units.literal: When terms were settled the various ministers discussed punishing the chief instigators; Ying Nian was stripped of office and sentenced to decapitation, detained in Xi'an prison, and soon granted suicide.

units.zh: 裕祿，字壽山，喜塔臘氏，滿洲正白旗人，湖北巡撫崇綸子。
units.en: Yu Lu, whose style was Shoushan, of the Xitala clan, came from the Plain White Banner; his father was Hubei Governor Chonglun.
units.literal: Yu Lu, styled Shoushan, of the Xitala clan, was a man of the Plain White Banner of the Manchus and son of Hubei Governor Chonglun.

units.zh: 以刑部筆帖式歷官郎中。
units.en: He rose from clerk in the Ministry of Justice to director.
units.literal: Starting as a clerk in the Ministry of Justice, he rose through the posts to director.

units.zh: 出為熱河兵備道，累遷安徽布政使。
units.en: He served as military intendant of Rehe, then rose to provincial treasurer of Anhui.
units.literal: He went out as military intendant of Rehe and was promoted step by step to provincial treasurer of Anhui.

units.zh: 同治十三年，擢巡撫，年甫逾三十。
units.en: In 1874 he was appointed governor at just over thirty.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi he was promoted to governor; he had just passed thirty.

units.zh: 前江南提督李世忠本降寇，罷職家居，所為橫恣，裕祿疏請誅之。
units.en: Former Jiangnan commander Li Shizhong, a former surrendered rebel living in retirement, behaved with violent arrogance; Yu Lu memorialized for his execution.
units.literal: Former Jiangnan Regional Commander Li Shizhong had originally been a surrendered bandit; dismissed and living at home, his conduct was violent and overbearing, and Yu Lu memorialized requesting his execution.

units.zh: 會以事詣安慶，召飲署中，酒行，出密旨，麾眾縛斬之，而仍卹其家，人以是高其能。
units.en: When Yu Lu visited Anqing on business, Li was summoned to the yamen; wine was served, a secret edict produced, and Li was bound and beheaded—yet his family still received relief, and people admired Yu Lu's resolve.
units.literal: When he happened to go to Anqing on business, Li was summoned to drink in the yamen; as the wine was served a secret edict was produced and the crowd was ordered to bind and behead him, yet his family was still granted relief; people therefore admired his ability.

units.zh: 光緒十三年，遷湖廣總督，調兩江，復還鄂。
units.en: In 1887 he became viceroy of Huguang, was transferred to the Two Jiangs, then returned to Hubei.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Guangxu he was transferred to Viceroy of Huguang, then to the Two Jiangs, and then returned again to Hubei.

units.zh: 廷議修鐵路，起盧溝訖漢口，下群臣議，裕祿力陳不可，忤旨。
units.en: When the court debated a railway from Lugou Bridge to Hankou, Yu Lu strongly opposed it and offended the throne.
units.literal: The court debated building a railway from Lugou Bridge to Hankou and referred it to all officials for discussion; Yu Lu strongly argued it could not be done and offended the throne.

units.zh: 十五年，徙為盛京將軍。
units.en: In 1889 he was transferred to general of Mukden.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year he was moved to be general of Mukden.

units.zh: 十七年，熱河奸民騷動，毀教堂，殺蒙人，裕祿會師朝陽，擊平之，予優敘。
units.en: In 1891 Rehe ruffians destroyed churches and killed Mongols; Yu Lu assembled troops at Chaoyang, suppressed them, and earned commendation.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year ruffians in Rehe stirred up trouble, destroyed churches, and killed Mongols; Yu Lu gathered troops at Chaoyang, struck and pacified them, and received preferential commendation.

units.zh: 二十年秋，朝鮮亂起，奉天戒嚴，坐安東、鳳凰失守，數被議。
units.en: In the autumn of 1894 Korean turmoil led to martial law in Fengtian; the loss of Andong and Fenghuang brought repeated censure.
units.literal: In the autumn of the twentieth year turmoil broke out in Korea and Fengtian was placed under martial law; because Andong and Fenghuang were lost he was repeatedly criticized.

units.zh: 明年，調福州，改授四川總督。
units.en: The following year he was posted to Fuzhou, then made viceroy of Sichuan.
units.literal: The next year he was transferred to Fuzhou and then appointed Viceroy of Sichuan.

units.zh: 二十四年，召為軍機大臣、禮部尚書兼總理各國事務衙門。
units.en: In 1898 he was recalled as grand councilor, Minister of Rites, and head of the Zongli Yamen.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned as Grand Councilor, Minister of Rites, and concurrently head of the Zongli Yamen.

units.zh: 會徵榮祿入樞廷，遂代之督直隸。
units.en: When Ronglu entered the Grand Council, Yu Lu replaced him as viceroy of Zhili.
units.literal: When Ronglu was summoned into the Grand Council, Yu Lu replaced him as Viceroy of Zhili.

units.zh: 義和拳起山東，入直境。
units.en: The Boxers rose in Shandong and entered Zhili.
units.literal: The Boxers rose in Shandong and entered Zhili territory.

units.zh: 初，義和會源出八卦教乾坎二系，聚黨直、魯間，為臨清郜生文餘孽，後稱團，專仇教。
units.en: The movement sprang from the Qian and Kan branches of the Eight Trigrams teaching, gathered followers in Zhili and Shandong, descended from Gao Shengwen of Linqing, and styled themselves militia devoted to anti-Christian violence.
units.literal: At first the Boxer association sprang from the Qian and Kan branches of the Eight Trigrams teaching, gathered followers between Zhili and Shandong, were remnants of Gao Shengwen of Linqing, and later styled themselves militia, specializing in hatred of Christianity.

units.zh: 裕祿初頗持正論，主剿，捕其酋姚洛奇置之法。
units.en: At first Yu Lu favored suppression, captured chieftain Yao Luoqi, and executed him.
units.literal: At first Yu Lu rather held correct views, favored suppression, captured their chieftain Yao Luoqi, and put him to the law.

units.zh: 逾歲，開州傳舉烽，言匪復至，擒渠率斬以徇。
units.en: A year later Kaizhou reported bandits returning; leaders were seized and beheaded as a warning.
units.literal: After a year Kaizhou reported beacon fires, saying the bandits had returned; the leaders were seized and beheaded as a warning.

units.zh: 居無何，毓賢撫山東，縱匪，匪散入河間、深、冀，而裕祿承風指，忽主撫。
units.en: Soon Yu Xian governed Shandong and indulged the Boxers; they spread into Hejian, Shenzhou, and Jizhou, and Yu Lu suddenly turned to appeasement.
units.literal: Before long Yu Xian governed Shandong and indulged the bandits; the bandits scattered into Hejian, Shenzhou, and Jizhou, and Yu Lu, following the prevailing wind, suddenly favored appeasement.

units.zh: 袁世凱方將武衛軍，語裕祿：「盍不請嚴旨捕治？」
units.en: Yuan Shikai, commanding the Wuwei Army, asked Yu Lu: "Why not request a stern edict to capture and punish them?"
units.literal: Yuan Shikai was then commanding the Wuwei Army and said to Yu Lu: "Why not request a stern edict to capture and punish them?"

units.zh: 裕祿曰：「拳民無他伎，緩則自消，激則生變。
units.en: Yu Lu replied: "The Boxers have no other arts; if handled gently they will fade, but provocation will breed disorder.
units.literal: Yu Lu said: "The Boxer people have no other skills; if treated gently they will dissipate on their own, but if provoked they will breed disorder.

units.zh: 且此委璅事，何煩瀆天聽邪？」
units.en: Besides, this petty matter hardly warrants troubling the throne."
units.literal: Moreover this is a petty trifling matter—why trouble Heaven's ear?"

units.zh: 已而毓賢去，世凱代之，自興兵疾擊，以故匪不敢近山東，而紛紛入畿疆矣。
units.en: Yu Xian departed and Yuan Shikai replaced him, striking hard so the Boxers avoided Shandong but flooded the capital region.
units.literal: Before long Yu Xian left and Yuan Shikai replaced him; he himself raised troops and struck swiftly, so the bandits did not dare approach Shandong but poured into the capital region.

units.zh: 吳橋知縣勞乃宣禁傳習，為書上裕祿，格不行。
units.en: Wuqiao Magistrate Lao Naixuan forbade Boxer practice and wrote to Yu Lu, but the letter was blocked.
units.literal: Lao Naixuan, magistrate of Wuqiao, forbade transmission and practice and wrote a letter to Yu Lu, but it was blocked and not carried out.

units.zh: 時直隸官吏多信拳，布政使廷杰獨力主剿辦，嚴定州縣查緝拳匪懲戒辦法。
units.en: Most Zhili officials then believed in the Boxers; only Provincial Treasurer Ting Jie insisted on suppression and laid down strict county-level measures to hunt and punish them.
units.literal: At that time most officials in Zhili believed in the Boxers; only the provincial treasurer Ting Jie alone insisted on suppression and strictly fixed methods for counties and prefectures to search out and punish the bandits.

units.zh: 遽奉詔開缺回京，匪愈橫。
units.en: An edict suddenly recalled him to Beijing, and the Boxers grew bolder still.
units.literal: He was suddenly ordered by edict to vacate his post and return to the capital; the bandits grew still more arrogant.

units.zh: 張德成居獨流，稱「舉國第一壇」，曹福田為津匪魁，二人者炫神術，為妄妖言相煽誘，裕祿不之問。
units.en: Zhang Decheng at Duliang styled himself head of "the foremost altar in the realm," and Cao Futian led the Tianjin Boxers; they traded boasts of magic and sedition, and Yu Lu looked the other way.
units.literal: Zhang Decheng dwelt at Duliang, styled "the foremost altar in the realm," and Cao Futian was chieftain of the Tianjin bandits; the two men boasted of divine arts and incited one another with wild demonic talk, yet Yu Lu did not question them.

units.zh: 已，复致書請餉二十萬，自任滅外人，裕祿馳檄召之，於是二人出入節署，與裕祿抗禮。
units.en: They soon demanded two hundred thousand taels, promising to destroy the foreigners; Yu Lu summoned them by urgent dispatch, and thereafter they came and went at his yamen as his equals.
units.literal: Before long they again wrote requesting two hundred thousand taels in funds, undertaking themselves to destroy the foreigners; Yu Lu sent urgent dispatches summoning them, and thereafter the two men came and went at the governor's yamen, treating him as an equal in ceremony.

units.zh: 當是時，津城拳匪至可三萬人，呼嘯周衢市，又以紅燈照熒眾，每入夜，家家懸紅燈，謂「迎仙姑」。
units.en: Boxers in the city may have numbered thirty thousand, roaring through the streets; the Red Lantern Society stirred the crowds, and every night households hung red lamps to "welcome the Immortal Maiden."
units.literal: At that time the bandits in the city may have reached thirty thousand; they roared through the streets and markets; moreover the Red Lantern Society inflamed the masses, and each night every household hung red lamps, saying they were "welcoming the Immortal Maiden."

units.zh: 頃之，各國兵艦大集，匪猶群聚督轅求槍砲，裕祿命詣軍械所任自擇，盡攫以去。
units.en: Soon foreign warships massed offshore, yet the Boxers still crowded the governor's yamen demanding arms; Yu Lu sent them to the arsenal to take what they wanted, and they carried everything away.
units.literal: Before long the warships of the various nations gathered in force; the bandits still thronged the governor's yamen demanding guns and cannon; Yu Lu ordered them to the arsenal to choose as they pleased, and they seized everything and left.

units.zh: 而聯軍絡繹登岸，索大沽砲台，裕祿懼，疏告急，請敕董福祥來援。
units.en: Allied troops landed in force and demanded the Taku forts; terrified, Yu Lu sent urgent memorials begging the throne to summon Dong Fuxiang.
units.literal: Meanwhile the allied armies landed in an unbroken stream and demanded the forts; Yu Lu was afraid, memorialized in urgent alarm, and requested an edict summoning Dong Fuxiang to aid.

units.zh: 聯軍索益堅，提督羅榮光不允，戰失利，而裕祿且上天津團民殺敵狀，於是朝廷以團民為可恃，宣戰詔書遂下，而不知大沽已先數日失矣。
units.en: The allies pressed harder; Commissioner Luo Rongguang refused and was defeated; yet Yu Lu also reported Tianjin militia victories, and the court, believing the militia dependable, declared war—unaware the Taku forts had fallen days earlier.
units.literal: The allied demands grew still firmer; Grand Commissioner Luo Rongguang refused; the battle was lost; yet Yu Lu also reported the Tianjin militia's kills of the enemy, and so the court believed the militia could be relied upon—the declaration of war was issued, not knowing the forts had already fallen several days before.

units.zh: 裕祿又報大捷，盛張拳匪功，發帑金十萬犒團，更薦德成、福田於朝，飾戰狀，獲賞頭品秩、花翎、黃馬褂。
units.en: He reported another great victory, lavished praise on the Boxers, distributed one hundred thousand taels to reward the militia, and recommended Decheng and Futian to the court with embellished battle accounts; they were given top rank, peacock feathers, and yellow riding jackets.
units.literal: He again reported a great victory, lavishly extolled the bandits' merit, issued one hundred thousand taels from the treasury to reward the militia, and further recommended Decheng and Futian at court, embellishing battle reports; they received rewards of top rank, peacock feather, and yellow riding jacket.

units.zh: 事急，官軍戰車站，敗績，裕祿退保北倉。
units.en: As the crisis deepened the regular army fought at the railway station, was routed, and fell back to Beicang.
units.literal: As matters grew urgent the regular army fought at the railway station, suffered defeat, and fell back to defend Beicang.

units.zh: 閱三日，城陷，德成、福田挾貲走，卒係而罪之。
units.en: Three days later the city fell; Decheng and Futian fled with their plunder but were eventually captured and punished.
units.literal: Within three days the city fell; Decheng and Futian fled with their loot, but in the end were seized and punished.

units.zh: 裕祿飛章自劾，詔革職留任。
units.en: Yu Lu urgently memorialized to impeach himself; the throne stripped his rank but left him in post.
units.literal: Yu Lu sent a flying memorial impeaching himself; an edict stripped him of office but kept him on duty.

units.zh: 踰月，北倉失，裕祿又退楊村，遂自殺。
units.en: A month later Beicang fell; he retreated to Yangcun and took his own life.
units.literal: After a month Beicang was lost; he retreated again to Yangcun, and then committed suicide.

units.zh: 廷雍，字邵民，滿洲正紅旗人。
units.en: Ting Yong, whose style was Shaomin, came from the Plain Red Banner of the Manchus.
units.literal: Ting Yong, styled Shaomin, was a man of the Plain Red Banner of the Manchus.

units.zh: 以貢生累官直隸布政使。
units.en: A senior licentiate, he rose to provincial treasurer of Zhili.
units.literal: A senior licentiate, he rose through the posts to provincial treasurer of Zhili.

units.zh: 裕祿死，護總督。
units.en: When Yu Lu died he served as acting governor-general.
units.literal: When Yu Lu died he acted as governor-general.

units.zh: 聯軍入保定，被執，並及諸士紳。
units.en: When the allies entered Baoding he was seized along with local gentry and scholars.
units.literal: When the allied armies entered Baoding he was seized, and gentry and scholars were implicated as well.

units.zh: 各軍訊其事，雍曰：「保紳夙從令，可釋，事皆由我。
units.en: The allied commanders interrogated him; Ting Yong said: "The Baoding gentry have long obeyed orders and may go free; the blame is mine alone.
units.literal: The various armies interrogated him about the affair; Yong said: "The Baoding gentry have long followed orders and may be released; the affair is all my doing.

units.zh: 今至此，斧鉞由汝，奚問為？」
units.en: I am here; the axe is yours—what more is there to ask?"
units.literal: Now that I have come to this, the axe is in your hands—why ask further?"

units.zh: 遂見殺。
units.en: He was then executed.
units.literal: He was then killed.

units.zh: 郡人尚多哀之。
units.en: Many in the prefecture mourned him.
units.literal: People of the prefecture still largely mourned him.

units.zh: 毓賢，字佐臣，內務府正黃旗漢軍。
units.en: Yu Xian, whose style was Zuochen, served in the Imperial Household Department as a member of the Plain Yellow Banner Han Chinese.
units.literal: Yu Xian, styled Zuochen, was of the Plain Yellow Banner Han Chinese in the Imperial Household Department.

units.zh: 監生。
units.en: He held student status at the Imperial University.
units.literal: A student of the Imperial University.

units.zh: 以同知納貲為山東知府。
units.en: He purchased office as subprefect and became prefect of Shandong.
units.literal: By purchasing office as subprefect he became prefect of Shandong.

units.zh: 光緒十四年，署曹州，善治盜，不憚斬戮。
units.en: In 1888 he served as acting prefect of Caozhou, suppressed bandits effectively, and did not shrink from executions.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he acted as prefect of Caozhou, was skilled at controlling bandits, and did not shrink from execution.

units.zh: 以巡撫張曜奏薦，得實授，累遷按察使，權布政使。
units.en: Governor Zhang Yao recommended him for substantive appointment; he rose to surveillance commissioner and acting provincial treasurer.
units.literal: Because Governor Zhang Yao memorialized recommending him, he received substantive appointment and was promoted step by step to surveillance commissioner and acting provincial treasurer.

units.zh: 二十四年，調補湖南，署江寧將軍。
units.en: In 1898 he was transferred to Hunan and acted as general of Jiangning.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Hunan and acted as general of Jiangning.

units.zh: 裁革陋規萬餘兩，上聞而嘉之。
units.en: He abolished corrupt customary fees exceeding ten thousand taels and earned imperial praise.
units.literal: He abolished corrupt customary fees totaling more than ten thousand taels; when the throne heard of it he was commended.

units.zh: 是時李秉衡撫山東，適有大刀會仇西教，秉衡獎借之，戕德國二教士。
units.en: Li Bingheng was then governor of Shandong; anti-Christian sentiment ran high in the Big Sword Society, and he encouraged it, resulting in the killing of two German missionaries.
units.literal: At that time Li Bingheng was governor of Shandong; there happened to be hostility toward Western religion in the Big Sword Society, and he encouraged and indulged it, killing two German missionaries.

units.zh: 廷議以毓賢官魯久，諳河務，擢代之。
units.en: The court judged Yu Xian's long service in Shandong and knowledge of river works qualified him, and appointed him in Li's place.
units.literal: The court considered that Yu Xian had long served in Shandong and understood river works, and promoted him to replace him.

units.zh: 既蒞事，護大刀會尤力。
units.en: Once in office he shielded the Big Sword Society more zealously than ever.
units.literal: Once he took up affairs he protected the Big Sword Society with especial force.

units.zh: 匪首朱紅燈搆亂，倡言滅教。
units.en: The rebel leader Zhu Hongdeng stirred up trouble and preached the extermination of Christianity.
units.literal: The bandit chieftain Zhu Hongdeng stirred disorder and preached destroying Christianity.

units.zh: 毓賢令知府盧昌詒按問，匪擊殺官軍數十人，自稱義和拳。
units.en: Yu Xian ordered Prefect Lu Changyi to investigate; the rebels killed dozens of government troops and proclaimed themselves the Boxer militia.
units.literal: Yu Xian ordered Prefect Lu Changyi to investigate; the bandits killed several dozen government troops and styled themselves the Boxer militia.

units.zh: 毓賢為更名曰「團」，團建旗幟，皆署「毓」字。
units.en: Yu Xian rechristened them "militia"; their banners all bore the character for his surname.
units.literal: Yu Xian renamed them "militia"; the militia raised banners, all marked with the character "Yu."

units.zh: 教士乞保護，置勿問。
units.en: Missionaries pleaded for protection; he ignored them.
units.literal: Missionaries begged for protection; he set the matter aside and did not inquire.

units.zh: 匪浸熾，法使詰總署，乃徵還。
units.en: As the movement spread, the French minister protested to the Zongli Yamen, and Yu Xian was recalled to Beijing.
units.literal: As the bandits grew daily more powerful, the French minister pressed the Zongli Yamen, and Yu Xian was recalled.

units.zh: 至則謁端王載漪、莊王載勛、大學士剛毅，盛言拳民忠勇得神助。
units.en: In Beijing he visited Prince Duan, Prince Zhuang, and Grand Secretary Gang Yi, praising the militia's loyalty, courage, and supernatural aid.
units.literal: On arrival he paid calls on Prince Duan, Prince Zhuang, and Grand Secretary Gang Yi, lavishly praising the people's loyalty, courage, and divine aid.

units.zh: 俄拜山西巡撫之命，於是拳術漸被山西。
units.en: He was soon appointed governor of Shanxi, and Boxer practices spread across the province.
units.literal: Soon he received appointment as governor of Shanxi, and thereafter Boxer arts gradually spread there.

units.zh: 平陽府縣上書言匪事，毓賢痛斥之，匪益熾。
units.en: Local officials reported on the Boxers; he rebuked them harshly, and the movement grew stronger.
units.literal: Prefectures and counties memorialized on the bandit situation; he rebuked them sharply, and the bandits grew still more powerful.

units.zh: 毓賢更命製鋼刀數百，賜拳童令演習，其酋出入撫署，款若上賓。
units.en: He ordered hundreds of steel blades forged for young boxers to practice with; rebel leaders came and went at his yamen, entertained like honored guests.
units.literal: He further ordered several hundred steel knives made and bestowed on boxing youths for drill; their chieftains came and went at the governor's yamen, entertained like honored guests.

units.zh: 居無何，朝旨申命保教民，毓賢陽遵旨，行下各縣文書稠疊，教士咸感悅。
units.en: Soon the court again ordered protection of Christians; Yu Xian ostensibly complied, flooding the counties with reassuring documents, and the missionaries were reassured.
units.literal: Before long an imperial order again commanded protection of Christian people; Yu Xian outwardly obeyed, sent down documents to every county in thick stacks, and the missionaries were all gratified.

units.zh: 未幾，又命傳致教士駐省城，曰：「縣中兵力薄，防疏失也。」
units.en: He then ordered missionaries brought to the provincial capital, saying: "County garrisons are too weak to protect you."
units.literal: Before long he again ordered missionaries summoned to stay in the provincial capital, saying: "In the counties military strength is slight and defense is lax."

units.zh: 教士先後至者七十餘人，乃扃聚一室，衛以兵，時致蔬果。
units.en: More than seventy missionaries arrived; he locked them in a single room under armed guard and sent them fruit and vegetables from time to time.
units.literal: More than seventy missionaries arrived one after another; he then shut them together in one room, guarded them with troops, and from time to time sent fruits and vegetables.

units.zh: 一日，忽冠服拜母，泣不可止，曰：「男勤國事，不復能顧身家矣！」
units.en: One day he appeared in full court dress before his mother, weeping uncontrollably: "I am consumed by affairs of state and can no longer protect our family!"
units.literal: One day he suddenly put on cap and robes and bowed to his mother, weeping without cease, saying: "Your son is laboring for state affairs and can no longer look after family and person!"

units.zh: 問之不語。
units.en: Asked what he meant, he would not answer.
units.literal: When asked he would not speak.

units.zh: 遽出，坐堂皇，呼七十餘人者至，令自承悔教，教民不肯承，乃悉率出斬之，婦孺就死，呼號聲不忍聞。
units.en: He rushed to the main hall, summoned the captives, and ordered them to renounce Christianity; when they refused, he had all of them beheaded—women and children among them—and their cries were unbearable.
units.literal: He rushed out, sat in the main hall, summoned the more than seventy persons, ordered them to confess repentance of Christianity; the Christians would not confess, and he then led them all out to be beheaded; women and children met death, and the cries were unbearable to hear.

units.zh: 聯軍既陷天津，毓賢請勤王，未及行，朝旨趣之再。
units.en: After Tianjin fell he asked to march to the emperor's aid; before he could depart, urgent orders from the court summoned him twice.
units.literal: After the allied armies took Tianjin he requested to come to the throne's aid; before he could set out, imperial orders urged him twice.

units.zh: 兩宮已西幸，毓賢遇諸塗，遂隨扈行。
units.en: The court had already fled west; he met the procession on the road and joined the flight.
units.literal: The two palaces had already gone west; he met them on the road and then followed the imperial procession.

units.zh: 和議成，聯軍指索罪魁，中外大臣復交章論劾，始褫職，戍新疆。
units.en: After peace was made the allies demanded the ringleaders; Chinese and foreign ministers memorialized again; only then was he stripped of rank and exiled to Xinjiang.
units.literal: When peace was concluded the allied armies pointed out and demanded the chief culprits; Chinese and foreign ministers again submitted joint memorials of impeachment; only then was he stripped of office and banished to Xinjiang.

units.zh: 十二月，行抵甘肅，而正法命下。
units.en: In the twelfth month, as he reached Gansu, the execution order came down.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, as he reached Gansu on the journey, the order for lawful execution was issued.

units.zh: 時李廷簫權甘督。
units.en: Li Tingxiao was then acting governor of Gansu.
units.literal: At that time Li Tingxiao was acting governor of Gansu.

units.zh: 廷簫，籍湖北黃安。
units.en: Li Tingxiao was a native of Huang'an in Hubei.
units.literal: Tingxiao was a native of Huang'an in Hubei.

units.zh: 以進士累官山西布政使，嘗附毓賢縱匪。
units.en: A jinshi, he rose to provincial treasurer of Shanxi and had once abetted Yu Xian in indulging the Boxers.
units.literal: A jinshi, he rose through the posts to provincial treasurer of Shanxi and had once abetted Yu Xian in indulging the bandits.

units.zh: 至是得旨，持告毓賢，毓賢曰：「死，吾分也，如執事何？」
units.en: He received the order and informed Yu Xian; Yu Xian said: "Death is my lot—what fault is yours?"
units.literal: At this time he received the order, took it and informed Yu Xian; Yu Xian said: "Death is my portion—what of your office?"

units.zh: 廷簫慮譴及，元旦仰藥死。
units.en: Fearing punishment, Li Tingxiao took poison on New Year's Day and died.
units.literal: Tingxiao feared punishment would reach him and on New Year's Day took poison and died.

units.zh: 蘭州士民為毓賢呼冤，將集眾代請命，毓賢移書止之。
units.en: Lanzhou gentry and commoners protested Yu Xian's innocence and were about to petition for his life; he sent a letter stopping them.
units.literal: Gentry and commoners of Lanzhou cried injustice for Yu Xian and were about to gather a crowd to plead for his life; Yu Xian sent a letter stopping them.

units.zh: 其母留太原，年八十餘矣。
units.en: His mother remained in Taiyuan, over eighty years old.
units.literal: His mother remained in Taiyuan, more than eighty years old.

units.zh: 一妾從行，令自裁。
units.en: One concubine accompanied him; he ordered her to kill herself.
units.literal: One concubine accompanied him on the journey; he ordered her to take her own life.

units.zh: 逾數日，伏誅未殊，連呼求速死，有僕助斷其頸，為斂而葬之。
units.en: Days later the execution had not finished him; he begged for swift death; a servant broke his neck, and he was buried.
units.literal: After several days execution had not yet finished him; he repeatedly cried out begging for swift death; a servant helped break his neck, and he was laid out and buried.

units.zh: 論曰：戊戌政變後，廢立議起，患外人為梗，遂欲仇之，而庚子拳匪之亂乘機作矣。
units.en: The historian comments: After the coup of 1898, the struggle over deposing the emperor revived; seeing foreigners as the obstacle, the court turned toward hostility, and the Boxer rising of 1900 erupted in that moment.
units.literal: The commentator says: After the coup of 1898, debate over deposing the emperor and installing an heir arose; fearing foreigners as an obstruction, they wished to make them enemies, and the Boxer disturbance of 1900 seized the opportunity to break out.

units.zh: 太后信其術，思倚以鋤敵而立威。
units.en: The Empress Dowager believed in their magic and hoped to lean on them to destroy enemies and assert her power.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager believed their arts and thought to rely on them to cut down enemies and establish authority.

units.zh: 王公貴人各為其私，群奉意旨不敢違，大亂遂成。
units.en: Princes and grandees each pursued private ends; all followed her will without dissent, and catastrophe followed.
units.literal: Princes, dukes, and nobles each pursued private ends; all followed her intent and dared not disobey, and great disorder was thus accomplished.

units.zh: 及事敗，各國議懲首禍，徐桐等皆不能免。
units.en: When the cause collapsed, the powers demanded the ringleaders be punished, and Xu Tong and his circle could not escape.
units.literal: When matters failed, the various nations discussed punishing the chief instigators, and Xu Tong and the others could none of them escape.

units.zh: 逢君之惡，孽由自作。
units.en: They had indulged the ruler's worst impulses; the ruin was of their own making.
units.literal: They indulged the ruler's wickedness; the calamity was of their own making.

units.en: Yet when punishments and rewards are dictated by foreign powers, what foundation remains for the state?
units.literal: Yet when punishment and reward obey others' commands, how can a state be established?
